name: home-hero
prompt: Professional documentary-style photograph, shot on a real full-frame DSLR with a 50mm prime lens, natural soft daylight (not studio strobes), true-to-life muted color grading, authentic depth of field, subtle film-like grain — must read as an unedited real photograph, never a 3D render or illustration. No text, no watermark, no logos. Rear three-quarter view: we see the back of a mason working on a brick facade, facing the wall, away from the camera. He wears a spotless, well-fitted work coverall in the company's brand colors — dark charcoal-anthracite as the main body color, with a terracotta-orange accent panel across the shoulders and a terracotta stripe down the side of the back, like clean professional branded workwear, no logos or text printed on it, no dirt or stains. He is mid-action, arm raised, pressing fresh mortar into a joint with a small trowel. IMPORTANT — this is mortar-joint (voegwerk) work only, never brick repair: the brick itself is completely intact, sound and undamaged everywhere in the frame (no cracks, no chips, no missing pieces, no old or weathered brick surface) — only the MORTAR JOINTS change condition. The left two-thirds of the wall (from the camera's point of view) already has clean, uniform, freshly finished mortar joints; the right third still has the old, weathered mortar joints (the brick there looks exactly as sound as everywhere else — only the joint mortar is old) — one clear, clean line where his completed work meets the remaining section. Dutch brick row houses softly out of focus in the background, natural overcast daylight, shallow depth of field.

name: voegwerk-closeup
prompt: Professional documentary-style photograph, shot on a real full-frame DSLR with a 50mm prime lens, natural soft daylight, true-to-life muted color grading, authentic depth of field, subtle film-like grain — must read as an unedited real photograph, never a render. No text, no watermark, no logos, no visible brand names. An extreme close-up filling the frame with several rows of professionally laid, perfectly straight, intact red-orange brick. IMPORTANT — this shows an in-progress voegwerk (mortar-joint) job, never brick repair, so the WALL CONDITION must clearly show three distinct joint stages side by side, left to right: (1) on the left, joints that have already been raked out (uithakken) — empty, clean grooves between the bricks with bare brick edges, old mortar fully removed, ready for new mortar, no crumbling debris left in them; (2) in the middle, a hand holding a small pointing trowel loaded with fresh grey mortar, actively pressing and smoothing it into one horizontal joint, mid-stroke; (3) on the right, joints that are already freshly finished — smooth, clean, uniform new grey mortar. Across all three stages and the entire frame, the brick itself stays completely intact, sound and undamaged (no cracks, no chips, no missing pieces, no old/weathered brick surface) — only the mortar-joint condition changes from section to section. Natural overcast Dutch daylight.
